Suspected vulnerabilities are not normal public bug reports. Confidential
security evidence belongs in [SECURITY.md](../../SECURITY.md), not in this
public issue. Use synthetic, minimal, or redacted evidence. Do not include
credentials, private user data, sensitive production traces, or unnecessary
full prompts/conversations.

Creating an issue does not authorize implementation. Maintainers classify the
change and identify the required specification, architecture, plan, evaluation,
security, and owner-review gates before implementation starts.

## Observed Behavior

What happened?

## Expected Behavior

What should have happened?

## Minimal Reproduction

List the smallest safe steps, inputs, fixtures, or commands that reproduce the
problem.

## Environment and Version

Record the environment, branch, commit, dependency version, browser, operating
system, or deployment context when known.

## Impact and Frequency

Who is affected, how often does it occur, and what capability is degraded?

## Safe Redacted Evidence

Attach or paste only redacted logs, screenshots, request IDs, stack labels, or
short excerpts that are safe for a public issue.

## Regression-test Expectation

Describe the test or evaluation evidence that should fail before the fix and
pass after the fix.

## Workaround

Name any known workaround and its limits.

## Rollback or Recovery Considerations

Describe any data, migration, deployment, or operational recovery concern.

## Scope

What is included in this bug fix request?

## Non-goals

What should remain outside this request?

## Acceptance Criteria

List observable criteria a reviewer can verify.

## Dependencies and Related Artifacts

Link related issues, specs, plans, ADRs, documents, experiments, or external
references.

## Maintainer Classification and Governance Routing

Maintainers record the change level, required spec, implementation plan,
architecture approval, ADRs, evaluation evidence, and repository-owner approval
gate here after intake review.
